papers.title: Expanded repeat RNAs drive aberrant cortical network activity in benign adult familial myoclonus epilepsy.
papers.title_zh: 扩增重复RNA驱动良性成人家族性肌阵挛癫痫中的异常皮层网络活动。
papers.abstract: Expansions of short nucleotide repeats cause diverse neurological disorders, yet how they perturb neuronal function remains unclear. Benign adult familial myoclonus epilepsy (BAFME) is caused by intronic pentanucleotide repeat expansions in genes including SAMD12. Here, we establish patient-derived cortical organoids and a microelectrode array platform, coupled with a frequency-decomposition-based analytical framework, to characterize BAFME-associated neuronal hyperexcitability and compare organoid electrophysiological features with those observed in patient electroencephalographic recordings. Single-cell RNA sequencing reveals altered expression of genes related to calcium regulation and α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) receptor function in BAFME cortical neurons. Consistent with these changes, BAFME organoids show an increased density of AMPA-receptor-positive synaptic puncta. Pharmacological AMPA receptor antagonism suppresses hyperexcitability. Antisense oligonucleotides targeting the expanded repeat RNA-which reduce pathogenic RNA foci without significantly affecting SAMD12 mRNA levels-also attenuate hyperexcitability. These findings indicate that targeting expanded repeat RNA mitigates aberrant cortical network activity in BAFME organoids.
papers.abstract_zh:
短核苷酸重复序列的扩增会导致多种神经系统疾病，但其如何扰乱神经元功能仍不清楚。良性成人家族性肌阵挛癫痫（BAFME）是由包括SAMD12在内的基因中内含子五核苷酸重复序列的扩增所致。在此，我们建立了患者源性皮层类器官和微电极阵列平台，并结合基于频率分解的分析框架，以表征BAFME相关……
神经元过度兴奋，并将类器官的电生理特征与患者脑电图记录中观察到的特征进行比较。单细胞RNA测序揭示了BAFME皮层神经元中与钙调节和α-氨基-3-羟基-5-甲基-4-异噁唑丙酸（AMPA）受体功能相关的基因表达发生改变。与这些变化一致，BAFME类器官显示出AMPA受体阳性细胞的密度增加。
e突触斑点。AMPA受体的药理学拮抗作用可抑制过度兴奋性。靶向扩增重复RNA的反义寡核苷酸（在不显著影响SAMD12 mRNA水平的情况下减少致病性RNA灶）也能减轻过度兴奋性。这些发现表明，靶向扩增重复RNA可减轻BAFME类器官中异常的皮层网络活动。

papers.title: Efficacy of Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation in Preventing Poststroke Spasticity: A Sham-Controlled Trial.
papers.title_zh: 重复经颅磁刺激预防卒中后痉挛的疗效：一项安慰剂对照试验。
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Poststroke spasticity significantly impairs recovery, yet preventive strategies remain limited. This study evaluated the effectiveness of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) in reducing the development and severity of spasticity in patients with early subacute stroke, offering a possible early intervention.
METHODS: In this double-blind, randomized, sham-controlled trial, 70 patients with early subacute stroke (7-30 days) were randomized to receive 3 sessions of low-frequency (1 Hz, 1000 pulses at 90% resting motor threshold) rTMS over contralesional primary motor cortex (n=35) or sham stimulation (n=35), alongside standard care. The primary outcome was upper-limb spasticity assessed using the modified Modified Ashworth Scale. Secondary outcomes included handgrip strength, muscle power assessed by the Medical Research Council scale, pain assessed by the Visual Analogue Scale, modified Rankin Scale, and Stroke Impact Scale 3.0.
RESULTS: rTMS therapy significantly lowered spasticity scores at 1 and 3 months across all assessed upper-limb joints (P=0.001), improved handgrip strength (P=0.01), and prevented pain (P=0.001). Stroke Impact Scale scores at 1 month showed greater gains in activities of daily living, mobility, hand function, social participation, and recovery in the rTMS group (P=0.001). Functional independence (modified Rankin Scale) was significantly better in the rTMS group (P=0.006) at 3 months. On binary logistic regression, sham stimulation was associated with greater odds of developing spasticity at 1 month (shoulder odds ratio [OR], 8.29 [95% CI, 1.95-35.27], P=0.04; elbow OR, 7.62 [95% CI, 1.69-34.35], P=0.08; wrist OR, 5.18 [95% CI, 1.60-16.78], P=0.06). At 3 months, sham stimulation remained predictive, with higher odds of spasticity at the shoulder (OR, 15.3 [95% CI, 8.26-28.43]), elbow (OR, 13.43 [95% CI, 3.94-45.78]), wrist (OR, 19.9 [95% CI, 4.9-80.96]), and fingers (OR, 26.25 [95% CI, 5.19-132.87], all P=0.001). Minor adverse events like headache and light-headedness were observed in 5 patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Low-frequency rTMS over contralesional primary motor cortex significantly prevented spasticity, improved motor recovery, reduced pain, improved functional outcomes and quality of life in early subacute stroke, supporting its role as a promising adjunctive therapy in early stroke rehabilitation.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://ctri.nic.in/; Unique identifier: CTRI/2024/01/061225.

papers.title: Calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) in epilepsy: Mechanistic insights from preclinical models.
papers.title_zh: 癫痫中的降钙素基因相关肽（CGRP）：来自临床前模型的机制见解。
papers.abstract: Calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) is a pleiotropic neuropeptide widely expressed in the central and peripheral nervous systems, with established roles in neurovascular regulation, synaptic transmission, and neuroinflammation. While CGRP has been extensively characterized in migraine pathophysiology, its role in epilepsy remains incompletely defined and is primarily supported by experimental evidence. Preclinical studies consistently demonstrate CGRP upregulation following prolonged seizures, particularly in models of status epilepticus, and suggest that CGRP signaling may contribute to key processes implicated in epileptogenesis. These include modulation of neuronal excitability, blood-brain barrier permeability, and neuroimmune responses, such as microglial activation. At the same time, CGRP has been shown to engage neuroprotective pathways, including anti-apoptotic and anti-oxidative mechanisms, as well as barrier-stabilizing effects, supporting a complex and context-dependent role. Shared pathophysiological features between migraine and epilepsy, such as cortical hyperexcitability, neuroinflammation, and cortical spreading depolarization, provide a conceptual framework in which CGRP may act as a convergent mechanistic mediator. However, direct evidence in human epilepsy remains limited, and the translational relevance of these findings requires careful interpretation. This review provides a focused synthesis of mechanistic insights from experimental models, highlighting the dual role of CGRP in seizure-related processes and delineating current gaps in knowledge. Potential clinical implications, including the effects of CGRP-targeting therapies, are discussed in a hypothesis-generating context, with emphasis on the need for rigorous studies to clarify their relevance in epilepsy. PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Migraine and epilepsy sometimes occur together and share changes in brain activity. This review examines CGRP, a signaling molecule involved in migraine, and its possible role in seizures. Animal studies suggest that CGRP can either increase abnormal brain activity and inflammation or protect nerve cells, depending on the conditions. Early observations in people raise the possibility that migraine medicines blocking CGRP could also affect seizures, but they do not prove a benefit. Further research is needed to determine whether these medicines can safely reduce seizures or prevent epilepsy.
papers.abstract_zh:
降钙素基因相关肽（CGRP）是一种多效性神经肽，在中枢和外周神经系统中广泛表达，在神经血管调节、突触传递和神经炎症方面具有公认的作用。虽然CGRP在偏头痛的病理生理学中已得到广泛阐明，但其在癫痫中的作用仍未得到完全确定，且主要有实验证据支持。临床前研究一致表明
在长时间癫痫发作后，CGRP表达上调，特别是在癫痫持续状态模型中，这表明CGRP信号传导可能对癫痫发生所涉及的关键过程有影响。这些过程包括神经元兴奋性的调节、血脑屏障通透性以及神经免疫反应（如小胶质细胞活化）。与此同时，CGRP已被证实可激活神经保护通路，包括抗凋亡和抗氧化通路。
机制以及屏障稳定作用，支持其发挥复杂且依赖于具体情况的作用。偏头痛和癫痫之间存在共同的病理生理学特征，如皮质过度兴奋、神经炎症和皮质扩散性去极化，这些特征提供了一个概念框架，其中CGRP可能充当一种汇聚性机制介质。然而，在人类癫痫中，直接证据仍然有限，而
这些发现需要谨慎解读。本综述重点综述了实验模型中对机制的认识，强调了CGRP在癫痫发作相关过程中的双重作用，并阐明了当前知识的空白。在提出假设的背景下讨论了潜在的临床意义，包括靶向CGRP疗法的作用，并强调需要开展严谨的研究来阐明其相关性。
在癫痫中的作用。通俗易懂的摘要：偏头痛和癫痫有时会同时发生，并且具有共同的大脑活动变化。本综述探讨了CGRP（一种与偏头痛相关的信号分子）及其在癫痫发作中可能的作用。动物研究表明，CGRP可以增加异常脑活动和炎症，也可以保护神经细胞，具体取决于具体情况。对人体的早期观察表明，偏头痛药物有可能
阻断CGRP也可能影响癫痫发作，但它们并未证明有益。需要进一步研究以确定这些药物是否能够安全地减少癫痫发作或预防癫痫。

papers.title: Subjective memory complaints and depressive mood in patients with epilepsy at the time of first seizure and one year later.
papers.title_zh: 癫痫患者在首次发作时和一年后的主观记忆障碍和抑郁情绪。
papers.abstract: Patients with epilepsy (PWE) often report subjective memory complaints (SMC) that reportedly do not thoroughly relate to 'objective' memory measures, but to depressive symptoms. While depressive symptoms appear to be involved very early in the disease, it is relatively unclear when SMC develop over the course of the illness. We examined two patient groups, namely PWE and patients, who had a first seizure (seizure patients, SP), but did not subsequently get the diagnosis epilepsy regarding factors influencing SMC scores at the time of the first seizure as well as one year later using regression analyses. These factors include a depressive symptom score, demographic and clinical variables. Additionally, we investigate the development of SMC and depressive symptoms over the time span of the first year after first seizure in both patient groups using analyses of variance (ANOVA). Regression analyses results revealed that depressive symptoms predicted subjective memory complaints at both time points. Group, based on diagnosed illness, did not predict an additional significant amount of variance. ANOVA results regarding SMC scores revealed that there were no systematic differences between patient groups and no significant development throughout the first year after first seizure. Results on depressive symptoms showed that PWE reported overall more depressive symptoms than SP. These findings hint towards the importance of monitoring depressive symptoms in epilepsy not only in patients who have had epilepsy for a long time, but also in newly diagnosed patients. Future studies are needed to investigate the beginning of SMC in epilepsy.
papers.abstract_zh:
癫痫患者（PWE）经常报告主观记忆障碍（SMC），据报道，这些障碍与“客观”记忆测量指标没有完全关联，而是与抑郁症状有关。虽然抑郁症状似乎在疾病的早期阶段就已出现，但SMC在疾病发展过程中的出现时间相对不明确。我们对两组患者进行了研究，即癫痫患者（PWE）和首次发作的患者（癫痫发作患者，SP），但未对……
使用回归分析，研究了在首次癫痫发作时以及一年后影响SMC评分的因素，这些患者随后被诊断为癫痫。这些因素包括抑郁症状评分、人口统计学变量和临床变量。此外，我们使用方差分析（ANOVA）研究了两个患者组在首次癫痫发作后第一年内SMC和抑郁症状的发展情况。回归
分析结果显示，在两个时间点，抑郁症状均可预测主观记忆力减退。基于诊断疾病的分组并未预测出额外的显著方差。SMC评分的方差分析结果显示，患者组之间不存在系统性差异，且在首次癫痫发作后的第一年内没有显著变化。抑郁症状的结果显示，PWE报告
总体上抑郁症状多于SP。这些发现表明，不仅要监测长期癫痫患者的抑郁症状，还要监测新诊断癫痫患者的抑郁症状。需要开展进一步的研究，以探究癫痫中SMC的起始。

papers.title: From potential to practice: An International survey on technology adoption and needs in epilepsy neuropsychology.
papers.title_zh: 从潜力到实践：一项关于癫痫神经心理学技术采用和需求的国际调查。
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Technological integration offers opportunities to improve neuropsychological practice in epilepsy care. Compared to other healthcare fields, neuropsychology has been relatively slow to incorporate these advancements into clinical practice.
OBJECTIVES: To describe the use of technology in epilepsy neuropsychology and identify priorities for technological development.
METHODS: An online survey of multiple choice and open-ended questions was developed in English and translated into Spanish, then sent to practicing neuropsychologists working in epilepsy care across all six International League Against Epilepsy world regions. The survey collected data on the settings in which neuropsychological services are provided to people with epilepsy, the technologies currently in use, the barriers to technological adoption, and desired future developments.
RESULTS: 179 neuropsychologists from 39 countries participated in the survey. The majority of respondents were women (69 %), aged 30-49 (60 %), and held a PhD (60 %). Key barriers to technological adoption included concerns around tool validation, financial limitations to purchase existing tools, and a lack of culturally and linguistically relevant normative data. Priorities for future development included predictive algorithms, automating psychometric aspects of clinical practice, and better leveraging of functional neuroimaging technologies.
CONCLUSIONS: This international survey highlights that while epilepsy neuropsychologists are open to adopting new technologies in their clinical practice, there are several barriers hampering uptake across the field. Survey responses highlighted that technological developments that are practical, accessible, evidence-based, and suitable for culturally and linguistically diverse populations are required to meet the needs of the epilepsy neuropsychology workforce.
papers.abstract_zh:
背景：技术整合为改善癫痫护理中的神经心理学实践提供了机会。与其他医疗保健领域相比，神经心理学将这些进步纳入临床实践的步伐相对缓慢。
目的：描述技术在癫痫神经心理学中的应用，并确定技术发展的优先事项。
方法：进行包含选择题和开放式问题的在线调查
该调查以英语编写并翻译成西班牙语，然后发送给在国际抗癫痫联盟（ILAE）所有六个世界区域从事癫痫护理工作的执业神经心理学家。该调查收集了有关向癫痫患者提供神经心理学服务的环境、当前使用的技术、技术采用的障碍以及期望的未来发展的数据。
结果：179名神经心理学家
来自39个国家的受访者参与了本次调查。大多数受访者是女性（69%），年龄在30-49岁之间（60%），并拥有博士学位（60%）。技术采用的主要障碍包括对工具验证的担忧、购买现有工具的资金限制，以及缺乏与文化和语言相关的规范性数据。未来发展的优先事项包括预测性算法、临床实践中心理测量方面的自动化
以及更好地利用功能性神经影像学技术。
结论：这项国际调查凸显出，虽然癫痫神经心理学家愿意在临床实践中采用新技术，但存在若干障碍阻碍了整个领域的采用。调查回复强调，实用、易于使用、循证且适合文化和语言多样性人群的技术发展
需要制定相关法规，以满足癫痫神经心理学从业人员的需求。

papers.title: Psychological interventions for functional/dissociative seizures: A systematic review.
papers.title_zh: 功能性/分离性癫痫发作的心理干预：一项系统综述。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Functional/dissociative seizures (FDS) have limited treatment options despite the major societal and personal impact of this condition. The efficacy of psychological interventions varies considerably and is influenced by social, economic, and personal factors. To guide future research on the condition, a systematic review of the published literature on the psychological treatments available for FDS was conducted. Current psychological interventions including diagnosis communication, psychoeducation, psychotherapy, hypnosis, and behavioural therapies have yet to show sufficient evidence of long-lasting successful treatment for FDS. The frequency and impact of FDS requires continued treatment development beyond the limited options currently available. Such treatments have been systematically reviewed for this purpose.
METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was carried out using the keywords: dissociative seizures, functional seizures, NEA, non-epileptic, pseudoseizures, psychogenic seizures, psychological treatment, hysterical seizures, and pseudoepileptic. Studies evaluating psychological treatments for FDS were included. Studies including patients with comorbid seizure disorders were also included.
RESULTS: A total of 55 studies (58 publications) met the inclusion criteria. A wide variety of psychological interventions for FDS have been investigated. Existing evidence suggests that several psychological interventions may be effective, with cognitive behavioural therapy demonstrating the strongest evidence base. Promising findings were also reported for diagnosis communication, psychoeducation, psychodynamic therapy, mindfulness-based therapy, behavioural therapy, and combined treatment approaches.
CONCLUSION: While a range of psychological treatments may be beneficial, cognitive behavioural therapy currently possesses the strongest evidence supporting its efficacy. However, no clear evidence suggests whether a particular intervention is most appropriate for specific patient subgroups. Structured diagnosis communication and psychoeducation appear to be valuable early interventions but may require additional psychological therapy to maintain treatment gains. Large studies of high methodological quality with longer follow-up periods are required to establish the most effective forms of treatment.

papers.title: Early-onset epilepsy and inborn errors of metabolism: A large retrospective pediatric cohort.
papers.title_zh: 早发性癫痫和先天性代谢缺陷：一项大型回顾性儿科队列研究。
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inborn errors of metabolism (IEM) are an under-recognised cause of childhood epilepsy. Early diagnosis is critical because specific treatments can substantially alter the disease course.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective study on 21,072 children evaluated for epilepsy in two Child Neurology referral centres in Eastern Sicily (i.e. Messina, Catania, and Enna) between January 2001 and December 2025. Medical records were reviewed to identify patients with a confirmed IEM diagnosis. Clinical, electrophysiological, neuroimaging, and treatment data were collected and analysed.
RESULTS: Fifty-seven children (0.27%) had a co-diagnosis of epilepsy and IEM (28 males, 29 females). Lysosomal storage disorders were the most common category (31.6%), followed by aminoacidopathies (22.8%), mitochondrial disorders (15.8%), congenital disorders of glycosylation (CDG, 12.3%), and organic acidaemias (7.0%). Seizure onset occurred before the age of three years in 83.3% of IEM cases, compared with 27.6% of children with non-metabolic epilepsy (OR 12.3; 95% CI 6.2-24.4; p < 0.001). Diagnostic delay exceeded 3.5 years from first seizure in half the cohort. Approximately 50% of patients showed drug-resistant epilepsy despite multi-drug anti-seizure medication therapy.
CONCLUSIONS: IEM should be systematically considered in any child presenting with epilepsy, particularly when onset occurs in the first three years of life. A structured stepwise diagnostic approach can substantially reduce diagnostic delay and facilitate access to disease-specific therapies.

papers.title: Ketogenic diet therapy in adults with status epilepticus: A systematic review.
papers.title_zh: 成人癫痫持续状态的生酮饮食疗法：系统综述。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically review evidence describing the use of ketogenic diet therapy in adults with status epilepticus.
METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant systematic review was conducted and registered in PROSPERO. MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception to June 13, 2025. Eligible studies included original research involving adults 18 years and older with status epilepticus treated with enteral or parenteral ketogenic diet therapy. Outcomes included ketosis, seizure control, mortality, functional outcomes, adverse events and ICU/hospital outcomes. Study quality was assessed using design appropriate tools.
RESULTS: Twenty-three studies comprising 123 adult patients were included, primarily of observational studies, case series, and case reports. Ketosis and seizure cessation were frequently reported, occurring in 79 % and 81 % of patients respectively. Reported median or individual times from ketogenic diet initiation and ketosis to seizure cessation ranged from two to 25 days and zero to 13.5 days respectively. Mortality among cohorts with deaths varied widely, overlapping with historically reported mortality for super-refractory status epilepticus. Neurological, cognitive, and patient-reported outcomes were infrequently assessed, and reporting of antiseizure medication or sedation-sparing effects were limited. Heterogeneity in study design, patient populations, diet protocols, ketosis monitoring, and outcome definitions precluded meta-analysis.
CONCLUSION: Evidence suggests an association between KD therapy and seizure cessation in adults with refractory and super-refractory status epilepticus, although evidence remains limited. While KD therapy requires careful management and adverse events have been reported, it remains a promising therapeutic strategy for this patient population. Prospective studies incorporating standardized outcome measures, ketosis monitoring, adverse-event reporting, and protocolized ketogenic diet implementation are needed to better define its role in this population.

papers.title: Prehospital recognition and differentiation of seizure presentations by paramedics and ambulance nurses: A scoping review.
papers.title_zh: 由辅助医务人员和救护车护士进行的院前癫痫发作表现的识别和鉴别：范围综述。
papers.abstract:
AIM: The aim of this scoping review was to identify and map the literature examining prehospital clinician recognition and differentiation of seizure presentations.
DESIGN: Scoping Review.
METHODS: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews. A literature search was conducted in January 2026 across five electronic databases.
DATA SOURCES: Medline, Emcare, ProQuest, CINAHL, and SCOPUS.
RESULTS: The search yielded 1264 citations, with 32 full-text articles assessed for eligibility and 18 studies included, six of them identified or re-assessed during peer review. Studies examined paramedics (n = 16) and ambulance nurses (n = 2), with the largest proportion of publications between 2019 and 2021. Across studies reporting diagnostic performance, measured against variable reference standards, sensitivity ranged from 54.0 to 58.5% and specificity from 95.9 to 96.6% using the principal diagnostic definitions reported. Recognition rates ranged from 56.8 to 89.7%, while non-recognition reached 55.3% in one study. Non-convulsive seizures were particularly challenging, with non-recognition rates of 53.0-81.4%.
CONCLUSION: This scoping review indicates that prehospital seizure recognition and differentiation remain suboptimal, particularly for non-convulsive presentations. However, variation in emergency medical services (EMS) workforce configurations and scope of practice limits generalisability across settings. Future research should prioritise outcomes-focused evaluations of seizure recognition and differentiation from key mimics.

papers.title: EEG-based Deep Learning Reveals Cortical Sensitivity to Small Changes in Deep Brain Stimulation Parameters.
papers.title_zh: 基于脑电图的深度学习揭示了大脑皮层对深部脑刺激参数微小变化的敏感性。
papers.abstract: Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) is an invasive procedure used to alleviate motor symptoms in Parkinson's Disease (PD) patients. Despite its effectiveness, the impact of DBS on brain activity and the way to optimise stimulation parameters remains unclear. In this study, we aimed to map the sensitivity of cortical neural response to changes in DBS parameters in real-world clinical settings. We recorded in-clinic EEG data from PD patients during their clinical DBS programming sessions, both at rest and during arm movement. A siamese variant of the EEGNet deep learning architecture was trained independently for each patient and parameter combination to determine whether two 1-sec-long EEG segments were recorded under the same or different DBS parameters, yielding 30 independently trained models. Our models achieved an average accuracy of 74% in classifying whether two 1-second EEG segments corresponded to the same or different DBS parameters. Explainability methods were then applied to extract the neural oscillations learned by the models. Ablation studies identified mid-gamma oscillations (55-90Hz) as the key band for classifying these changes. Importantly, that was not driven by 1:2 gamma entrainment. In a sub-group of patients, the theta-alpha oscillations (4-12Hz) also contributed to detecting changes in DBS parameters. We demonstrate that small DBS parameter changes modify cortical activity in a consistent manner that can be detected using shallow convolutional networks on low-density EEG. Our findings suggest that cortical mid-gamma oscillations (55-90Hz) are highly sensitive to small changes in DBS settings. Our approach and findings could be leveraged towards identifying and defining novel digital biomarkers to guide DBS programming and adaptive DBS systems.

papers.title: Developmental Aspects of Language Mapping with Stereoelectroencephalography.
papers.title_zh: 立体脑电图语言定位的发育方面。
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society
papers.abstract: This review examines developmental perspectives on the use of stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) for delineating language areas and networks in pediatric patients with drug-resistant epilepsy, both as a clinical tool for presurgical evaluation and as a modality for gaining neuroscientific insights into speech and language development. Language development is a dynamic process that begins before birth and continues into adulthood, shaped by the maturation of brain networks. SEEG allows high-resolution study of these networks, providing a unique perspective on the organization of language systems. This review traces language acquisition from early infancy through adolescence and adulthood, highlighting the pivotal role of neural oscillations. We then summarize classical and contemporary neural models of language organization, highlighting the distributed and hierarchical networks, and emphasize the high spatial and temporal resolution of SEEG for presurgical planning that enables clinicians to optimize neurosurgical interventions while preserving essential language areas and the tracts connecting them. Our review also addresses the human brain's remarkable plasticity and capacity for reorganization, which are especially pronounced in children and vital for adaptation to and recovery from neurologic injury or surgery. We focus specifically on developmental reorganization in pediatric patients with drug-resistant epilepsy and its implications for language mapping with SEEG. The review concludes with recommendations for designing language-mapping batteries tailored to the unique needs of pediatric patients.

papers.title: Characteristics of EEG Microstate Analysis of Power Grip and Precision Grip Hand Movements from Motor Planning to Execution.
papers.title_zh: 从运动计划到执行的握力和精细握力手部运动的脑电微状态分析特征。
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
papers.iso_journal: IEEE Trans Neural Syst Rehabil Eng
papers.abstract: Hand movement is a fundamental daily motor behavior. Precision grip and power grip reflect distinct post-stroke recovery stages and neuroplasticity, making their neural mechanisms critical for motor control and neurorehabilitation. This study employed electroencephalographic (EEG) microstate analysis to investigate neural dynamic characteristics during motor planning and execution stages between precision grip (two-finger pinch, TP) and power grip (hand clenching, HC). High‑density EEG was acquired from 24 healthy participants across TP, HC, and resting states. Separate microstate analyses were conducted using an event-related potentials (ERP)-based approach for planning and an EEG‑based approach for execution. Results showed that nine ERP microstate templates identified during planning shared identical temporal sequences for both grips, with significantly longer duration of the fourth microstate (MS4) in TP than HC. During execution, four canonical microstates (MSA, B, C, and D) were extracted, which are generally associated with auditory processing, visual processing, default-mode network, and executive attention, respectively. Compared with HC, TP induces stronger suppression of MSC, greater activation of MSD, and distinct transition probabilities with enhanced shifts from MSA, MSB and MSC to MSD. Classification accuracy was higher in the execution stage, with Random Forest reaching 72.07% for TP versus rest. These findings indicate that precision and power grip present consistent temporal sequences of microstate templates during planning but undergo task-specific neural regulation during execution. Precision grip requires more extensive planning processing and stronger suppression of non-motor networks. This study reveals the spatiotemporal neural dynamics underlying different grip types, providing potential biomarkers for motor decoding and advancing neurorehabilitation and brain - computer interface applications.

papers.title: Conductive Hydrogels for Invasive Neural Interfaces: From Materials Engineering to Neural Signal Interfacing and Neurorehabilitation.
papers.title_zh: 用于侵入式神经接口的导电水凝胶：从材料工程到神经信号接口和神经康复。
papers.abstract: In invasive neural interfaces, mechanical mismatch between traditional rigid electrodes and brain tissue often leads to inflammation and signal attenuation. Conductive hydrogels have emerged as ideal alternative materials due to their tissue-matching modulus, hybrid conductive networks, and wet adhesion properties. In this paper, we provide a narrative review of research progress on conductive hydrogels in invasive neural interfaces: we elucidate electronic, ionic, and hybrid conduction mechanisms; critically compare strategies for modulus matching and interfacial adhesion (such as catechol chemistry and covalent anchoring); and summarize their applications in neural signal recording, electrical/optical modulation, and rehabilitation for spinal cord injury and stroke. Finally, we discuss current challenges regarding long-term stability, wireless integration, and intelligent closed-loop systems and outline future directions involving AI-driven design combined with 3D biomanufacturing.

papers.title: Safety of responsive neurostimulation in pediatric and young adult patients with drug-resistant epilepsy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.title_zh: 对药物难治性癫痫的儿童和青年患者进行反应性神经刺激的安全性：系统综述和荟萃分析。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Responsive neurostimulation (RNS) is increasingly being used for pediatric drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE), but the safety of the procedure in children remains unclear. The authors systematically reviewed published clinical outcomes in pediatric RNS, with an emphasis on complications and other adverse events.
METHODS: The authors performed a PRISMA-guided systematic review and meta-analysis. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through August 12, 2025. They included observational studies reporting outcomes of RNS in patients aged ≤ 21 years at implantation and extractable pediatric data. Two authors independently screened articles and extracted data. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients experiencing at least 1 complication. A sensitivity analysis restricted to extractable patients aged ≤ 18 years was also performed.
RESULTS: Thirty-five studies met inclusion criteria, representing 358 pediatric patients who underwent RNS implantation. Most studies were case series (62.9%), followed by case reports (25.7%) and cohort studies (11.4%); all were conducted in the United States. The mean patient age at implantation was 14.8 years, and the mean follow-up was 20.3 months among studies reporting follow-up. Overall, 38 patients experienced at least 1 complication. The most frequently reported complications were infection (3.4%), transient neurological deficits (3.1%), return to the operating room (2.2%), and explantation (2.0%). Less common events included stimulation-related side effects (1.4%), CSF-related complications (1.1%), and wound dehiscence and device malfunction (0.6% each). Random-effects meta-analysis demonstrated a pooled overall complication proportion of 10.3% (95% CI 7.0%-14.9%; I2 = 0.0%). In the ≤ 18-year sensitivity analysis, 31 studies comprising 203 patients were included, with a pooled complication proportion of 8% (95% CI 4%-16%).
CONCLUSIONS: Published pediatric RNS experience suggests that complications are comparable to rates reported for similar procedures and are most often transient neurological symptoms, reoperation, or infection. However, the evidence base is largely limited to small observational reports with heterogeneous outcome definitions and high risk of bias. Higher-quality multicenter prospective studies with standardized reporting and longer follow-up are needed to better define safety and effectiveness of RNS in pediatric DRE. Systematic review registration no.: CRD420261339088 (https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/).

papers.title: Causal Evidence for Emotion-Selective Neural Populations Supporting Emotion Perception in the Human Third Visual Pathway.
papers.title_zh: 支持人类第三视觉通路中情绪感知的情绪选择性神经元群体的因果证据。
papers.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract: The posterior superior temporal sulcus (pSTS) is central to social perception, but whether it contains emotion-selective neural populations that causally contribute to emotion recognition in humans remains unknown. Here, we used state-dependent cortico-cortical paired associative stimulation (ccPAS) to test whether emotion-selective populations within the human pSTS→V1/V2 re-entrant pathway can be selectively strengthened via Hebbian-like plasticity. Sixty participants received ccPAS targeting either backward (pSTS→V1/V2) or forward (V1/V2→pSTS) projections of the third visual pathway while viewing fearful or happy faces; only one emotion was temporally paired with stimulation. pSTS→V1/V2 ccPAS selectively improved recognition of the paired emotion, with no effects on the unpaired emotion or following V1/V2→pSTS stimulation. These findings provide causal evidence that spatially overlapping, but functionally distinct, emotion-selective neural populations within the human pSTS-V1/V2 pathway make specific contributions to emotion recognition, such that ccPAS strengthening of one population selectively improves recognition of its preferred emotion, highlighting the functional relevance and selective malleability of human pSTS-V1/V2 circuits for emotion recognition.

papers.title: Brain-computer interfaces for neurodegenerative diseases: A comprehensive review of closed-loop systems from diagnosis to neural rehabilitation.
papers.title_zh: 用于神经退行性疾病的脑机接口：从诊断到神经康复的闭环系统综合综述。
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interface (BCI) technology serves as an important bridge between the nervous system and external devices and has shown considerable promise for the diagnosis and treatment of neurodegenerative diseases, whose global burden continues to increase: in 2021, more than 57 million people were living with dementia worldwide, with Alzheimer's disease (AD) accounting for approximately 60-70% of cases, while an estimated 11.77 million people were living with Parkinson's disease (PD) in 2021, according to the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021. This growing disease burden, together with the progressive loss of cognitive, motor, and communicative functions, highlights the need for more precise approaches to early detection, functional assistance, and individualized intervention. Conventional diagnostic and therapeutic approaches remain poorly suited to early detection and timely intervention. This paper analyzes the development of BCI technology, from the first detection of electroencephalogram (EEG) signals to the parallel development of invasive and non-invasive systems, and outlines the basic principles of signal acquisition, processing, and decoding, together with the relative advantages and limitations of different approaches. It then focuses on the use of BCI in Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), covering early diagnosis, functional reconstruction, and neuromodulation. The article also discusses the difficulties encountered by BCI technology in terms of technological realization, clinical translation, and ethical considerations, as well as several future research directions, including multimodal fusion, adaptive algorithms, closed-loop control systems, and personalized treatment so as to drive the applications of BCI in precision medicine and in neurological diseases.

papers.title: Optogenetics in neurobiology and neurodegenerative disorders: from neural circuit mechanisms to precision neuromodulation.
papers.title_zh: 神经生物学和神经退行性疾病中的光遗传学：从神经环路机制到精准神经调节。
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative disorders, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, Huntington's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, multiple sclerosis and stroke, are characterized by progressive neuronal dysfunction, synaptic impairment and neural circuit degeneration, leading to severe cognitive and motor deficits. Although considerable progress has been made in understanding their molecular pathology, the circuit level mechanisms driving disease onset and progression remain incompletely understood. Optogenetics, which combines microbial opsins, genetic engineering and optical stimulation, enables reversible, cell-specific control of neuronal activity with millisecond precision and has transformed neuroscience from observational analysis to causal investigation of neural circuits. This review summarizes recent advances in the molecular basis of optogenetics, microbial opsins, gene delivery strategies and optical stimulation technologies, together with their applications in basic neurobiology and neurodegenerative disease research. We discuss how optogenetics has advanced understanding of neural circuit organization, synaptic plasticity, memory, neurodevelopment, sleep regulation, protein aggregation, synaptic dysfunction, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial impairment, oxidative stress and regulated cell death. Although these studies have generated important mechanistic insights and demonstrated functional improvements in experimental models, translation into human therapies remains investigational due to challenges associated with gene delivery, long-term opsin expression, immune compatibility and optical accessibility. Emerging therapeutic strategies, including closed-loop neuromodulation, wireless photostimulation, artificial intelligence-assisted neural decoding, nanotechnology enabled light delivery and brain computer interfaces, are critically evaluated with emphasis on their current evidence status, translational challenges and limitations for clinical implementation. Collectively, optogenetics provides an unprecedented platform for deciphering disease mechanisms and evaluating circuit-based neuromodulation strategies, while continued technological and biological validation will determine its future role in precision therapies for neurodegenerative disorders.

papers.title: A translational platform for brain-computer interfaces and adaptive neuromodulation: Technical characterization, long-term validation, and implementation of the CorTec brain interchange-BCI2000 ecosystem.
papers.title_zh: 脑机接口和自适应神经调节的转化平台：CorTec脑交换-BCI2000生态系统的技术表征、长期验证和实施。
papers.abstract: Adaptive neuromodulation systems and implantable brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) are promising therapies for neurological and psychiatric disorders. However, their broader translation into research and clinical practice remains limited by technological complexity, restricted access to implantable research platforms, and the lack of standardized, reproducible experimental workflows. We therefore aimed to develop and validate an open, general-purpose translational ecosystem that enables rapid development, evaluation, and dissemination of novel neuromodulation and implantable BCI paradigms.Approach: The CorTec Brain Interchange (BIC) implantable neural sensing and stimulation device was integrated with the open-source BCI2000 platform to create a modular, extensible neuromodulation ecosystem. We established a standardized battery of quantitative assessments to characterize implantable neuromodulation systems to comprehensively evaluate the CorTec BIC device through benchtop characterization, long-term preclinical in vivo validation, and a human feasibility demonstration using the benchtop BIC system connected to externalized leads.Results: Comprehensive benchtop characterization of the BIC device independently validated previously reported performance while extending its evaluation through quantification of recording noise, acquisition and stimulation latencies, and validation of impedance measurements. Long-term in vivo validation in five canines, with the longest implantation exceeding three years, demonstrated stable chronic recordings while also capturing progressive deterioration of individual channels through longitudinal changes in signal quality and impedance. The ecosystem enabled active functional decoding more than two years after implantation, closed-loop stimulation using arbitrary spectral biomarkers, capturing brain stimulation evoked potentials, detection of epilepsy-associated biomarkers and observational assessment of their response to stimulation. In addition, we translated an established one-dimensional BCI cursor-control paradigm to the BIC benchtop system, demonstrating ecosystem portability and feasibility with a human participant. Finally, we share surgical protocols, imaging and analysis pipelines, datasets, and software to facilitate reproducible neuromodulation research.Significance: We present a versatile, open-source translational ecosystem that supports a wide range of neuromodulation and implantable BCI applications with minimal modification. By combining comprehensive hardware characterization with standardized software tools and experimental workflows, this work provides a practical reference for researchers adopting the BIC platform while establishing a broadly applicable framework for systematic characterization of implantable neuromodulation systems. The ecosystem lowers technical barriers to implantable neurotechnology research, promotes reproducibility, and provides a foundation for accelerating the development and clinical translation of next-generation adaptive neuromodulation and implantable BCI therapies for patients with neurological and psychiatric disorders.

papers.title: Micro-magnetic stimulation for neuromodulation: technological evolution from discrete inductors to MEMS and wireless passive systems.
papers.title_zh: 用于神经调节的微磁刺激：从分立式电感器到MEMS和无线无源系统的技术演变。
papers.abstract: Micro-magnetic stimulation (µMS) has emerged as a pivotal paradigm, providing high spatial precision and temporal resolution while eliminating direct electrode-tissue interactions. This review systematically traces the technological evolution of µMS systems, from discrete-inductor prototypes to high-precision MEMS-based micro-coils, array architectures, and wireless passive stimulators. Fabrication strategies, including standard MEMS and heterogeneous integration, are compared, and the impact of coil geometry on field focalization and selectivity is examined. The strategic transition from wired active driving to wireless passive operation, facilitated by resonant WPT and multi-frequency resonant compensation (MFRC) networks, is highlighted. Recent breakthroughs in FDMA and autonomous power allocation for multi-site targeting are discussed. Persistent challenges include the scaling limits of passive units, inter-channel crosstalk, and the mechanistic complexity of broadband neuromodulation. Future advances will focus on sub-millimeter-scale integration, power-signal co-optimization, and intelligent closed-loop neural interfaces for next-generation, large-scale neuromodulation systems.

papers.title: Acute central metabolic effects of otolithic vestibular stimulation in a non-human primate model of Parkinsonism: proof-of-concept neuroimaging and functional study.
papers.title_zh: 在帕金森病非人灵长类动物模型中，耳石前庭刺激的急性中枢代谢效应：概念验证性神经影像学和功能学研究。
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vestibular dysfunction has increasingly been recognized in the pathophysiology of Parkinson's disease (PD), particularly in relation to postural instability, gait impairment, and altered sensorimotor integration. However, the central metabolic effects associated with acute targeted otolithic vestibular stimulation remain poorly understood.
OBJECTIVES: To explore the acute metabolic correlates associated with otolithic vestibular stimulation using 18F-FDG PET in a non-human primate model of PD following vestibular implantation.
METHODS: A unilateral otolithic vestibular implant was placed in a macaque (Macaca fascicularis) with MPTP-induced Parkinsonism. Parkinsonian severity and persistence of motor impairment were descriptively assessed using repeated blinded Kurlan motor scale evaluations and standardized fine motor performance tasks. Longitudinal 18F-FDG PET imaging was performed during four experimental stages: basal pre-MPTP condition, MPTP-induced parkinsonian state before implantation, and one- and two-month post-implantation evaluations. Post-implantation PET acquisitions were obtained under OFF and ON stimulation conditions. Voxel-wise subtraction analyses were performed to characterize relative metabolic differences across experimental stages and stimulation conditions.
RESULTS: MPTP administration induced a persistent parkinsonian phenotype characterized by marked deterioration in fine motor performance relative to baseline, together with persistently elevated Kurlan motor scores throughout follow-up. Metabolically, the MPTP-induced condition was associated with relative hypermetabolism involving especially audiovestibular cortical areas, accompanied by relative hypometabolism in frontal executive, paralimbic, and visual associative regions. Acute vestibular stimulation (ON vs. OFF) demonstrated state-dependent metabolic differences across post-implantation evaluations. During stimulation, increased metabolism predominantly involved vestibulo-thalamo-striatal, sensorimotor, and limbic-paralimbic networks. In contrast, OFF conditions showed relatively greater involvement in visual associative cortices and cerebellar vermis.
CONCLUSION: Acute otolithic vestibular stimulation was associated with metabolic modulation of vestibulo-thalamo-striatal and sensorimotor-related networks in a parkinsonian non-human primate model. These findings provide proof-of-concept evidence supporting the capacity of vestibular neurostimulation to engage distributed central motor integration circuits.
